title: Attorney General of Maryland

context.text: Anthony Brown (D) and James Rutledge III (R) are the two candidates listed for the November 3, 2026 general election by the Maryland State Archives.
Neither nominee had a primary opponent on June 23, 2026: Brown received 568,685 votes in the Democratic primary and Rutledge 161,800 in the Republican primary.

candidates.name: Anthony G. Brown
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary unopposed.

priorities.text: Continuing the office's legal challenges to Trump administration policies; he said the office files only actions "that involve the things that Marylanders talk about around the kitchen table," such as threatened transportation and education funding.
Police accountability through the office's Independent Investigations Division, which he said, alongside body-worn cameras, is part of "the accountability and oversight that's necessary."

positions.summary: Defended Maryland's law barring the sale and transfer of pistols that can be easily converted into machine guns after a federal court declined to block it.
positions.quote: Maryland has the right to protect its communities from weapons that can be rapidly turned into machine guns.

statements.quote: We are filing this lawsuit not just to protect Maryland today, but to protect the Maryland our loved ones will inherit tomorrow.
statements.context: On joining a 25-party lawsuit challenging EPA's repeal of greenhouse gas limits on power plants

record.text: Defended Senate Bill 334, Maryland's law prohibiting the sale and transfer of machine-gun-convertible pistols beginning January 1, 2027; a federal judge denied the plaintiffs' motions for a preliminary injunction.
Joined a coalition of 25 states, counties and cities in a petition in the D.C. Circuit challenging the EPA's repeal of 2024 power-plant greenhouse gas standards.
Joined a coalition of 26 state and local governments suing the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration in the First Circuit over its final rule weakening fuel economy standards.

Announced that a federal court in Oregon permanently blocked federal SNAP-related fines on states and guidance restricting food assistance for lawful permanent residents, in a multistate suit Maryland joined in November 2025.
Announced Maryland's participation, as co-lead with other attorneys general, in a $694 million multistate settlement with Credit Acceptance Corporation over auto loans.

candidates.name: James B. Rutledge III
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the June 23, 2026 Republican primary unopposed.

priorities.text: Saying the Attorney General's office should not sue the federal government over policy disagreements: "We need to focus on Maryland, and litigating against Washington, D.C., or the powers that be in Washington, shouldn't be a knee-jerk reaction."
Greater support for law enforcement, including backing a Fraternal Order of Police-endorsed proposal on how officers are placed on prosecutors' "do not call" lists.
Stronger action to protect the Chesapeake Bay watershed, including against waste dumped into the Susquehanna River by other states.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website could be located; positions come from a Maryland Matters interview (Oct. 2026). No direct statements on the fixed issue list were found. No elected record beyond the Bel Air commission term.
